source.summary: Portable C/C++/Rust or matching-decomp source -> Emscripten/LLVM -> WebAssembly.

n64.summary: Prefer N64Recomp/decomp. Ogre Battle 64 proves a real Emscripten path; renderer coverage is still game/microcode-specific.

gamecube.summary: CPU/AOT and WebGPU renderer core exist; Emscripten browser platform/surface host is the current gap.

wii.summary: Same core path as GameCube; browser platform integration remains engineering work.

ps2.summary: Play! officially builds with Emscripten and ships an experimental browser frontend; no external BIOS is required because it uses HLE BIOS.

psp.summary: Community PPSSPP WebAssembly/Emscripten fork with a browser shell and COOP/COEP server; not an official PPSSPP release.

ps1.summary: RetroArch has an official Emscripten frontend. Use a PS1 libretro core that supports the web target; Beetle PSX has Emscripten-specific code paths.

nes.summary: RetroArch Web Player + an Emscripten-compatible NES core such as FCEUmm.

snes.summary: RetroArch Web Player + an Emscripten-compatible SNES core.

gba.summary: RetroArch Web Player + an Emscripten-compatible GB/GBC/GBA core such as mGBA.

genesis.summary: RetroArch Web Player + an Emscripten-compatible Genesis/Mega Drive core.

pc32.summary: For older 32-bit Windows games, use matching-decomp/recomp-kit where compatible; recomp-kit demonstrates Emscripten/WebGPU/pthreads/WasmFS.

other.summary: Look for source/decomp/static-recomp first, then a mature emulator core with an Emscripten/browser target.
